title: Edge-to-core pattern catalog — onboarding primer (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working primer intended to help Solutions Eng and Private Deployments run onboarding sessions for customers with hybrid edge-to-core VPC architectures. Focus: patterns that balance low-latency edge inference for customer gateways, centralized core model serving, and secure, auditable Terraform-driven provisioning.

Status and scope:
- Draft: experimental patterns validated in 2 lab customers (telecom pilot, healthcare PoC).
- Not a finalized playbook — contains open questions and tactical options to present during kickoff.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineering, Field SREs, Customer Network Engineers, Customer Success leads.

High-level patterns (summary):
1) Push-edge + core-pool (recommended for low-latency reads)
   - Edge: small fleet (1–4 GPUs / region) colocated near customer endpoints for token-level latency sensitive inference (quantized models, local KV cache).
   - Core: central Dedicated capacity pool with autoscale and higher-capacity GPUs; used for heavy/backfill requests, model retraining, and large-batch workloads.
   - Routing: smart routing policy (edge-first, fallback-to-core).
   - Terraform notes: edge stacks use lightweight module: tf-edge-gw (network + peering + service endpoint), core stacks use tf-dedicated-cluster (autoscaling groups, placement groups, SGs). Ensure modules expose a "preferred_route_priority" var.

2) Transit-gateway-backed segmentation (recommended for strict tenancy/isolation)
   - Use cloud TGWs (or equivalent on-prem routers) to centralize egress and inspection.
   - Each tenant gets a segmented VPC with enforced egress via a central inspection VPC.
   - Terraform pattern: single reusable module for route propagation and attachments; ensure idempotent creation of attachments (common failure in previous runs).

3) Air-gapped core with edge sync (regulated workloads)
   - Core runtime sits in an air-gapped environment (on-prem), edges operate in customer VPCs and synchronize model artifacts over approved transfer channels (signed artifacts + checksum).
   - Terraform: split-state approach (separate state backends for air-gapped modules). Document manual steps for cert rotation and artifact publishing.

Quick onboarding checklist (kickoff -> cutover):
- Pre-kickoff (Solutions Eng): collect CIDR ranges, expected qps/latency SLA, compliance constraints, KMS/HSM requirements. Create JIRA record and link to this doc.
- Design workshop (1–2 hours): review pattern options (push-edge vs transit), present estimated cost/latency tradeoffs and fallback flows.
- Terraform baseline delivery: run terraform plan in staging account; share plan output with customer SRE and obtain approval for routing changes.
- Staging validation: deploy to staging VPC, validate peering/TGW attachments, exercise failover (simulate core outage and verify edge fallback).
- Cutover: coordinate maintenance window, run apply in production state, monitor health checks and token-level latency (console hooks).

Tf module pragmatics and observed pitfalls:
- Idempotency: modules that create TGW attachments in loops can race — prefer separate attachment resource with explicit depends_on in root module.
- State drift on route tables: route propagation can be slow; include a small wait-and-verify step in the runbook to assert propagation before cutover.
- Secrets & certs: use customer-managed KMS keys where required; provide an optional module var to reference an existing KMS key ARN instead of creating a new one.
- Provider pinning: lock provider versions in module registry to avoid subtle behavior changes during upgrades.

Operational playbook snippets (for SRE on call):
- Edge overloaded?
  - Mitigation: enable core-burst routing (increase priority to core for 5–10m), scale core pool, and increase batching window on edge to reduce per-token cost.
- Connectivity flaps between edge and core?
  - Immediate: route to local cached model variant, log samples for postmortem, raise ticket with network team.
- Drift detected after TF apply?
  - Run terraform refresh, diff against desired state; if manual changes are responsible, recommend import into state or revert manual edits.

Integration test ideas (before customer sign-off):
- Latency SLO test (p95 < target): synthetic workload from edge lambda -> edge node, measure token turnaround.
- Failover test: shut down core endpoint for 30s and assert no more than 1%) increased error rate during window and automatic fallback occurs.
- Security posture: validate egress rules, run an automated scan on Terraform plan for any overly permissive SGs.

Open questions / decisions to finalize:
- Model variant policy: whether customers prefer deterministic fallback to a quantized variant (faster, lower quality) or probabilistic sampling to preserve quality. TODO: poll three pilot customers.
- Centralized logging level: compressed vs full token payloads (privacy concerns). Need legal sign-off for healthcare customers.
- Standardizing TGW vs direct peering: which path reduces ops overhead for multi-region tenants?

Reference commands and snippets:
- Example: verify route propagation (AWS):
  aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=resource-type,Values=vpc | jq .
- TF workaround for attachment idempotency (root module): include explicit resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment" with name var and depend_on to avoid concurrent deletes.

Post-deploy retrospective items (collect for each onboarding):
- Actual sustained qps and p95 latency from edge/core.
- Token-cost delta after enabling caching/batching.
- Any manual network changes performed by customer that weren't captured in TF.
- One-line summary for product (3 bullets) to feed into onboarding playbook index.

Appendix: lab-run notes (short)
- Telecom pilot: used push-edge + core-pool, observed 18% lower p95 when edge cache hit rate > 65%. Main friction: customer's existing NOC wanted control over BGP adjacency; solved by documented BGP peer matrix and pre-approved ASN list.
- Healthcare PoC: opted for air-gapped core; extra manual step required for artifact signing and transfer — plan to add helper script to tf-modules repo.

Action items (short):
- Lina: write the tf-module PR to add explicit attachment resource and provider pin (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- Diego: schedule a 90-min design workshop template and create a slide template for customers.
- Ava: collect three pilot responses on model fallback preference and update this doc by 2026-03-01.

Notes to self:
- Keep this document minimal and link to deeper runbooks for step-by-step terraform commands.
- When happy with the pattern decisions, convert to a canonical playbook in Confluence and mark this Drive doc as archived.
